title: Regional Sales Director, Strategic Enterprise - UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"><strong>Who we are</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 300; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 300; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.</span></p></div><p><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p>Samsara’s UK Enterprise business is one of our fastest-growing segments globally. We’ve scaled rapidly over the past several years — consistently outpacing the broader business — and we’re now at an inflection point where we need to pair that momentum with operational rigour to sustain growth at scale. </p> <p>This Regional Sales Director role is central to that next chapter. You’ll lead a team of six Senior Enterprise Account Executives and Client Directors selling into some of the UK’s largest and most complex organisations, spanning transportation, logistics, infrastructure, utilities, and field services. </p> <p>The team is performing — but we want to turn strong results into a repeatable, scalable engine. That means bringing structure, coaching discipline, and a proven enterprise playbook without losing the pace and builder energy that got us here.</p> <h4><strong>In this role, you will:</strong><span style="font-weight: 400;"> </span></h4> <ul> <li>Own the performance, development, and day-to-day leadership of a team of Senior Enterprise AEs, driving net new logo acquisition and expansion across a defined set of strategic UK accounts</li> <li>Coach your team through complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles where average contract values regularly reach seven figures over multi-year terms</li> <li>Build and run a structured operating rhythm - pipeline reviews, deal inspection, forecasting discipline - while getting close enough to the detail to add value at the deal level</li> <li>Develop your reps’ ability to access economic buyers, build multi-threaded relationships, and position Samsara’s expanding product portfolio against a customer’s most critical business priorities</li> <li>Pressure-test deal qualification, challenge assumptions, and help your team navigate the complexity of selling into large UK enterprises - this isn’t a role where you sit above the deals</li> <li>Build the commercial muscles - cross-sell, multi-product attach, stakeholder mapping - that will drive durable growth as we expand our footprint across the UK’s largest accounts</li> <li>Partner closely with the AVP of Strategic and Enterprise Sales UK, your peer RSDs, and cross-functional teams including Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Marketing to ensure your team has the support it needs to win</li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team</span></strong></li> </ul> <p><strong>Minimum requirements for the role:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven experience as a frontline or second-line sales leader in B2B enterprise technology, with direct responsibility for team quota attainment</li> <li>Track record of coaching Account Executives through complex, multi-quarter sales cycles with average deal sizes of £250K+ ACV, but with experience of seven figure ACV deals </li> <li>Experience selling into large, multi-stakeholder organisations where procurement, legal, and multiple business units are involved in the buying decision</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to build and enforce a structured sales operating cadence — pipeline generation, deal qualification, forecasting accuracy, and stage progression</li> <li>Strong commercial instinct for multi-product or platform selling, where the value proposition spans multiple use cases and buyer personas</li> </ul> <p><strong>An ideal candidate also has:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience at a high-growth technology company that was scaling its enterprise go-to-market in the UK or EMEA — ideally where you helped build or refine the playbook rather than inheriting an established one</li> <li>A coaching-first leadership style with a track record of developing AEs from good to exceptional, not just managing top performers</li> <li>Experience managing forecast accuracy as a discipline, not just an output — particularly in an environment where leadership investment decisions depend on the reliability of your calls</li> <li>Comfort operating in a fast-moving, scaling organisation where not everything is perfectly defined yet, and where you’re expected to build process while delivering results</li> <li>A blend of strategic thinking and tactical intensity — you can set a multi-year account strategy and also jump into a deal review and tell a rep exactly where their qualification is weak</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Total Rewards</strong></p> <p>At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why <a href="https://www.samsara.com/company/careers/benefits">our rewards</a> are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.</p> <p>Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.</p> <p><strong>Flexible Working </strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.</span></p> <p><strong>Belonging at Samsara</strong></p> <p>At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.</p> <p><strong>Accommodations </strong></p> <p>Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email <a ---------- or <a href="https://forms.gle/DrM6DFQUiSgfPtCVA">click here</a> if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.</p> <p><strong>Our Commitment to Authenticity</strong></p> <p>We use <a href="https://hiretofu.com/privacyPolicy">Tofu</a>, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s <a href="https://www.samsara.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice">Candidate Privacy Notice</a> for more information.</p> <p><strong>Fraudulent Employment Offers</strong></p> <p>Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in ----- ----- or ----- For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our <a href="https://samsara.com/blog/avoiding-fake-job-offers">blog post here</a>.</p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Product Manager
description: <p>This is an<strong> initial 6-month fixed-term contract</strong> for <strong>those based in the UK</strong> and authorised to work without sponsorship. This position also <strong>requires travel to client sites</strong>, with travel expenses covered by the company.</p> <p><strong>About Nearform</strong></p> <p>Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.</p> <p>Our deep expertise in solving the world's most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.</p> <p>Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media O2, and Walmart.</p> <p>As part of our Product function, our Senior Product Managers play a crucial role in translating business vision into successful digital products that drive enterprise success and enhance customer experiences. They define and execute product strategy, balancing high-level vision with hands-on operational execution. In a Product role at Nearform, you will collaborate closely with client stakeholders, engineers, and designers to uncover and define requirements, ensuring a deep understanding of user needs to shape the product roadmap. With a strong focus on strategy, communication, and delivery, you will guide teams in building impactful, scalable solutions that align with business goals and market demands.</p> <p><strong>About the Senior Product Manager role</strong></p> <p>As a Senior Product Manager, you will be a strategic visionary who oversees the development and execution of complex digital products. You'll collaborate closely with clients to define product vision, drive product strategy, translate goals into actionable roadmaps, and oversee the entire product lifecycle. Based on client goals, you will lead complex products and/or a portfolio of products. However, as you'll likely work on a variety of projects, your responsibilities may also include:</p> <ul> <li>Translate business strategy into product strategy and execute that strategy in the delivery phase with the engineering team(s) </li> <li>Collaborate with stakeholders to define the product roadmap </li> <li>Lead the ideation, development, and launch of features </li> <li>Drive action throughout the organisation to get products to market </li> <li>Plan and carry out product launches, MVPs, and phased releases </li> <li>Provide insight to stakeholders on the product, competitors, technical innovations, and market </li> <li>Provide product marketing with insights on key differentiators and messages </li> <li>Write requirements - typically as epics, features, and user stories — including clear acceptance criteria </li> <li>Define and adhere to Definition of Ready and Definition of Done</li> <li>Support grooming and refinement ceremonies in collaboration with Tech Leads to ensure alignment on the requirements and to support the delivery goals </li> <li>Identify, document, and communicate risks, changes, or delays as soon as possible</li> <li> Manage all aspects of in-life products, including customer feedback, requirements, and issues </li> <li>Participate in daily scrum meetings, planning, reviews, demos, and retrospectives </li> <li>Collaborate with client teams</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we are looking for</strong></p> <ul> <li>Significant experience delivering at a senior level, including experience in defining product-level OKRs </li> <li>You will typically have at least 3 years' experience delivering commercial impact at scale</li> <li>Demonstrable experience in leveraging AI in day-to-day product operations</li> <li>Demonstrable idea-to-launch product experience</li> <li>Product-level ownership (not feature or journey level)</li> <li>Hands-on experience delivering products in an agile environment, collaborating directly with engineers and designers </li> <li>Experience with early-stage products, new product development, and product modernisation from discovery to MVP launch and beyond </li> <li>Proven ability to collaborate with senior stakeholders at various levels (C-Suite, VP, Director) and areas of the organisation, with differing business goals, to drive successful roadmaps and releases. You may have previously played a Head of Product or equivalent role. </li> <li>Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with product experience and mature judgement </li> <li>The ability to define and lead product discovery workshops to define customer journeys, deliver tangible roadmaps and a prioritised backlog, including test-and-learn and A/B testing methodologies </li> <li>Demonstrable experience in delivering business and customer outcomes </li> <li>Excellent communication and collaboration skills</li> <li>Professional proficiency in English</li> </ul> <p><strong>Our Interview Process</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Talent Call</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>(30 mins via Zoom)<br>An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.</li> </ul> <hr> <ul> <li><span class="Apple-converted-space"><strong>Product Interview</strong> </span>(1 hour via Zoom)<br>An in-depth discussion with up to two of our trained Product Management interviewers to find out more about your experience, your preferred ways of working, and how you would solve some of the problems our Senior Product Managers face when dealing with clients.</li> </ul> <hr> <ul> <li><span class="Apple-converted-space"><strong>Product Case Study</strong> (1 hour via Zoom)</span><br>As the final step, you'll complete a short product case study and present your recommendation during the interview, followed by questions and discussion. The call will focus on your product thinking, decision-making, and ability to work through assumptions and unknowns. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.</li> </ul> <p><em>There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project</em></p> <p><strong>Ready to Join Us?</strong></p> <p><em>If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we'd love to hear from you.</em><em>Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.</em></p> <p><em>Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built on respect, inclusivity, diversity, and excellence.</em></p> <p><em>If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.</em></p> <p>Our<strong> salary range starts at £85,000 </strong>+ benefits. Further details will be discussed in the initial interview, and final compensation will be determined based on skills, experience, and other job-related factors discussed during the interview process.</p> <p> </p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Product Manager, Enterprise Deployment Solutions |  UK | Remote
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at <u><span><a href="http://grafana.com" target="_blank">grafana.com</a></span></u> and follow us on <u><span><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/grafana-labs/" target="_blank">LinkedIn</a></span></u> and <u><span><a href="https://twitter.com/grafana" target="_blank">X</a></span></u><u>.</u></p> <p>We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.</p> <p>You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.</p></div><p> </p> <p>This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in the UK.</p> <h2>About Product Management</h2> <p>As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own the experience for your product as well as its roadmap and competitive positioning, and you will collaborate with company leadership on setting your product's goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.</p> <p>Product Managers are the bridge that connects R&D to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.</p> <h2>The role</h2> <p>As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you'll own the Grafana Labs offerings that run outside our standard multi-tenant SaaS. That includes <strong>Grafana Federal Cloud</strong>, for organizations that need FedRAMP-authorized observability: US federal agencies; state, local, and education (SLED) customers; and commercial companies that sell FedRAMP offerings of their own. It also includes <strong>Grafana Cloud Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)</strong>, which delivers the full Grafana Cloud experience while the customer pays the infrastructure bill directly to their cloud provider, saving them significantly at scale.</p> <p>Your mission is to make Grafana Labs the obvious choice for organizations that can't use standard SaaS because of compliance, data, or cost-at-scale constraints. Deployment choices change the product: features that are simple in standard SaaS can be hard, expensive, or impossible in a regulated or customer-owned environment. You’ll be responsible for adapting existing Grafana Cloud capabilities to these environments, deciding which features come in, which wait, and which stay out, and occasionally building something specific to BYOC or Federal Cloud. You'll also help shape which deployment models we offer next.</p> <p>Along the way, you’ll use AI tools daily to speed up research, analyze product signals, and develop positioning, applying strong judgment to the results.</p> <p>As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you will: </p> <ul> <li>Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Grafana Bring Your Own Cloud and Grafana Federal Cloud products, using product data and market research to balance customer value against engineering cost and technical constraints</li> <li>Own positioning, messaging, and differentiation for these products, including how they compare to regular Grafana Cloud, and partner with Product Marketing on launches, competitive analysis, enablement, and demand programs</li> <li>Partner with Engineering and Technical Program Management on buildouts for these environments, balancing customer timelines with engineering capacity</li> <li>Work directly with customers, prospects, and the field on strategic deals and brief partners, resellers, and analysts on our deployment options</li> <li>Partner with Security, Compliance, and Legal to work through product changes affecting our authorization or existing customer commitments</li> </ul> <h2>We’re excited about you because you have</h2> <ul> <li>5+ years of product management experience on a technical B2B product, <em>or</em> a technical background (software engineering, solutions architecture, SRE, or technical program management) plus a demonstrated move into product ownership</li> <li>Hands-on experience with a non-standard SaaS deployment model, such as self-managed, air-gapped, sovereign, BYOC, single-tenant, or FedRAMP/government cloud, and a firsthand understanding of how it changes the product, its operations, and its economics</li> <li>Experience with cloud infrastructure, platform software, or developer tools</li> <li>Clear product and go-to-market judgment: you've shaped what a product should be and how it's positioned and sold, not only when it ships</li> <li>Interest in working with US public sector customers and learning their needs and buying cycles. Deep compliance expertise isn't required.</li> <li>Experience leading across multiple teams without direct authority, with excellent written and verbal communication in a remote, globally distributed organization</li> </ul> <h3>Bonus Points</h3> <ul> <li>Experience selling to or building for US federal, state, or local government customers, or other highly regulated industries</li> <li>Familiarity with government or sovereign cloud frameworks, such as FedRAMP, StateRAMP/GovRAMP, BSI C5, or SecNumCloud, or with offerings such as AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, or GCP Sovereign Cloud</li> <li>Experience with pricing and packaging across deployment models</li> <li>Experience with observability, monitoring, or other data-intensive infrastructure products</li> <li>Experience working with resellers, systems integrators, or cloud marketplace partners</li> <li>Familiarity with open source software or commercial open source companies</li> </ul> <p><em data-stringify-type="italic"><em>In the UK, the base compensation range for this role is GBP <span data-sheets-root="1">117,949</span><span data-sheets-root="1">-  GBP 141,539</span>. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. title: Staff Software Engineer - AI
description: tl;dr After 14 years in construction tech, Lea & Jonas are building the AI foundation for the construction industry 6 of Europe's 20 largest construction companies already rely on Kuro, with leading construction enterprises representing over €40bn in combined annual construction volume using the platform every day Construction has some of the most complex, unstructured data you can throw at an LLM. At Kuro, you can tackle some of the hardest problems in applied AI every day Curious about the bigger engineering challenge? Explore the vision and open problems at kuro.build . About us Lea and Jonas scaled two of Europe's leading construction tech companies - Capmo and alcemy - and saw firsthand the challenges holding the industry back. Now they're tackling the root cause: the 50% of construction work still lost to manual data handling. Kuro is building the AI foundation for construction. We're reimagining how construction professionals get work done and make decisions by leveraging AI to augment back-office workflows and make core data accessible. We are not pursuing marginal improvements, but a step change for construction. After one year on the market, leading construction enterprises with a combined annual construction volume of >€40 billion use Kuro every day to automate workflows and make faster, better decisions. Backed by an €10 million seed round, we already process more than 1 million pages every month and expect that volume to grow 10x over the next six months. We are 15 people based in Berlin. You will join a group of technical ex-founders and builders who are ambitious and kind. Learn more: Join Kuro - Berlin What You'll Do Set the technical direction Own the architecture decisions for the platform, from document ingestion to the chat UI Write and review RFCs. The technical roadmap for the next two to three quarters is yours. Make the build-or-buy decisions: which models we use, and which retrieval and orchestration stack we build on. Turn a vague customer request (“show me where the bid deviates from the BoQ”) into a scoped plan with the risks named. Raise the bar for the team Mentor engineers: Review their designs and their code. Define the engineering standards. Find what slows the team down, in tooling or in the CI/CD pipeline, and fix it. Interview and hire engineers. You have no direct reports. You change decisions in product and in other teams with a written argument. Build and own end-to-end (AI) features Design and implement new features to solve a specific user problem, such as document versioning or our agentic Chat. From concept to DB schema, to optimizing LLMs, to UI. Own the full development lifecycle of customer-facing features. Manage evaluations and scoring, and perform error analysis on new and shipped AI features. Build the platform that abstracts workflow building Contribute to the workflow harness, decision-trace standard, and eval tooling so a new use case ships in ~1 month Build reusable human review & approval surfaces where trust in AI output is earned Work on the construction ontology & project graph Help model and evolve canonical entities of our customers Contribute to entity resolution across sources: recognizing the same requirement, position, or price across BoQs, contracts, drawings, and bids Build features so answers are evidence-linked and auditable, and decisions flow back into the graph Contribute to scalable data pipelines & integrations Extend our multi-modal ingestion of unstructured documents - PDFs, scans, drawings, and 3D models - orchestrated and cost-efficient at scale Build read/write integrations with customer systems (document management, ERP/AVA), so workflows complete work end-to-end Projects you would be involved in Current & Past projects Project & document versioning guaranteeing data lineage in construction projects German tokenizer for construction-specific search Document pipeline ingesting 10,000s of PDFs per day Native BIM/DWG file support: ingesting and processing 3D models Design the ontology v1 + graph schema: core construction entities, evidence links, and per-customer extension model Build out our workflow harness to run agentic workflows for customers Current Tech Stack It is still day 0 for Kuro. Therefore, we are highly pragmatic with our tool choices. We believe in keeping it simple and moving quickly. You significantly help shape our tech stack decisions. Web-App: Typescript Database / Vector DB and File Storage: AWS RDS / Trubopuffer / AWS S3 Backend: Fastify API + Prisma ORM Workflow Orchestrator: Prefect (Python) Hosting: AWS Elastic Beanstalk AI: Azure / OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, AWS Obsv., Eval. & Tracking: Langfuse, Datadog Your profile This is the perfect role for an experienced engineer who wants to join an early stage company that builds a high impact applied AI product Bring 6+ years of experience as a Staff (full-stack) software engineer or Technical Lead, in a fast-paced environment Have proven experience delivering production-grade applied AI features to customers Take full ownership of solving customer problems by designing and implementing AI features Thrive in a small, accountable team with a high degree of ownership and a drive to make an impact Communicate fluently in both spoken and written English Enjoy working onsite with the team at our office in Factory Berlin Mitte every day Bonus Points You’ve started a company before or worked at a very early stage startup You built side projects in the past - we’re excited to hear about these! German-speaking (definitely not a must, we’re fully international) Why Kuro You’ll join at a point when customer demand is proven, but our product and platform are still yours to shape. You’ll own customer-facing features end to end while building the foundations beneath them, from ingestion pipelines and workflow infrastructure to our construction ontology and project graph. As Kuro grows, you can grow with it, whether as a leading individual contributor, technical leader or people manager. The Process Talent Acquisition Call – Intro, motivation, logistics & fit (30 min) Impact Interview – Deep dive into your experience, ownership & impact (60 min) On-site Day System Design – Designing under ambiguity & LLM craft (45 min) AI-Native Coding – Hands-on coding with AI (45 min) Final Culture Interview (approx. 60 min) Reference calls Decision Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Engineer
description: About Andercore Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry. Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell. We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought. We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded. Where we are today: Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth. About the role Andercore runs global trade end to end, from sourcing and pricing to sales, logistics and financing, and AI agents do a growing share of that work. Order values are high and prices and stock change daily, so the systems underneath have to be fast, correct and reliable at all times. As a Staff Engineer, you own our hardest technical problems and set the architecture across teams. You focus on what a fast-growing trading business cannot afford to get wrong: speed, reliability, security and observability. You report to our VP Engineering and work closely with our Senior Product Engineers, QA and product managers. You stay hands-on: you write code, review designs and raise the bar for everyone around you Tech stack Java 21 and Spring Boot 3, Python, LangGraph and LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), PostgreSQL, Kinesis, AWS with Terraform, GitHub Actions, and TypeScript with Node.js, Next.js and React. Including Salesforce, which we are moving our transaction core out of. What you will do Set the technical direction across teams: define the target architecture, write the RFCs behind big decisions, and make sure teams build towards the same picture. Lead the hardest technical work yourself, from design to production, instead of only advising on it. Shape the carve-out of our transaction core from Salesforce into a modern, modular core system, with a migration path that never disrupts daily trading. Make reliability, security and observability part of how we build: monitoring, alerting, incident response and postmortems that lead to real changes. Design how our AI agents act safely on money-touching paths, with evaluations, guardrails, audit trails and human review where it matters. Set standards for correctness and data integrity, including idempotency, validation and testing, together with QA. Mentor engineers through design reviews, pairing and direct feedback, and help us hire by defining what great engineering looks like at Andercore. In your first six months, you might Design the architecture of our pricing engine so it scales with a growing assortment and more markets, and serves correct prices to sales, and later directly to customers, in milliseconds. Lay out the target architecture and first steps for moving our transaction core off Salesforce. Build the observability and incident setup that lets us catch problems before customers or colleagues notice them What you bring At least 8 years of experience building and running software in production, including systems where errors cost real money. Deep backend expertise at production scale in Java or a comparable language such as Kotlin, C# or Go, and willingness to work in Java and Spring Boot. A track record of setting architecture across several teams, through influence rather than a management title. Experience designing transactional, distributed and event-driven systems, with a strong focus on correctness, failure modes and performance. Hands-on depth in reliability, security and observability, and experience leading incidents and postmortems. Experience in a fast-growing company, and a track record of solving business problems, not only technical ones. AI is part of your daily work. Experience building or evaluating AI agents in production is a strong plus. Experience with re-platforming or carving out systems from a platform like Salesforce or an ERP is a plus Practical details Location: Berlin, hybrid Working language: English A learning budget for your development Start date: As soon as possible We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. title: Field Service Engineer – Semiconductor Equipment (f/m/d)
description: Description Our quantum sensing technology is already operating in customer environments across Taiwan, the United States, and Europe. As our installed base grows and we move from first deployments to repeat orders, ensuring the reliability and performance of every system becomes increasingly important. As our Field Service Engineer, you'll take hands-on ownership of our systems throughout their operational lifecycle — from installation and commissioning to preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair. You'll work directly with leading semiconductor foundries, IDMs, and OSATs, ensuring our systems operate reliably and consistently meet their specifications. You'll collaborate closely with our Engineering and Applications teams, combining technical problem-solving with a strong customer focus. This is also an opportunity to help shape our global service function from an early stage, introducing the processes, tools, and standards that will support our growing international installed base. Who we are Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing. Why join Quantum Diamonds? Picture this: Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide. Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday. Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on. An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you. Still unsure about why joining us? You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before. From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds. Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years. You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors. Let’s make the invisible visible! What will you do Install, commission, and qualify our quantum sensing systems at customer sites across Europe, the US, and Asia, working closely with our Munich-based engineering teams. Perform preventive maintenance, calibration, troubleshooting, and repairs across optical, laser, mechanical, electronic, and software subsystems. Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues systematically, collaborating with Engineering and R&D when deeper technical expertise is required. Take ownership of system reliability and technical service, working closely with Field Application Engineers who focus on measurement execution and customer applications. Manage spare-parts availability for your installed base, including inventory tracking, consumption planning, replenishment, and coordination of service logistics. Document service activities, technical findings, and root causes, feeding recurring issues and improvement opportunities back into Product Development. Build trusted relationships with customers by providing clear technical communication, reliable support, and professional service in demanding semiconductor environments. Help establish and continuously improve our global service processes, including maintenance procedures, troubleshooting guides, documentation, and training materials. What is expected of you 3+ years of hands-on experience as a Field Service Engineer, Equipment Engineer, or in a comparable technical service role, ideally working with semiconductor, optical, laser, inspection, or metrology equipment. Strong practical troubleshooting skills across complex electromechanical systems, ideally combining optics, lasers, precision mechanics, electronics, and control software. Experience working in semiconductor fabs, cleanrooms, or similarly demanding technical environments, with an understanding of relevant safety and operating procedures. Familiarity with laser safety and interlocked systems, or willingness to complete the necessary technical and safety qualifications. Experience with spare-parts management, service documentation, and ERP or service ticketing systems is an advantage. A structured, independent, and solution-oriented approach to technical challenges, even when working under time pressure. Strong communication skills and a customer-focused mindset, with the ability to explain technical issues clearly and build trust with different stakeholders. Willingness to travel internationally for approximately 80% of your working time, primarily supporting customer installations across the US, Europe, and Asia. Fluency in English; German, Mandarin, Japanese, or Korean would be a plus. A degree in Engineering, Physics, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent technical training and relevant practical experience. Our benefits Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual. Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast. Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active. Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment. Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired. Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills. Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together. About us QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act. DNA goes in, characterized proteins come out, and a customer gets results in days rather than the months a CRO would take. Everything that machine consumes — synthesized genes, reagents, consumables, biosensors, catalog proteins — is something we buy, on lead times we do not control. It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business. So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet. You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. One thing makes it harder than a typical procurement job: our assay portfolio keeps expanding, and every new assay brings new reagents. You are not optimizing a static supply chain, you are building one that flexes with the science. How far the role goes from there is up to you. What You'll Do Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot. De-risk the supply chain. Too much of what we depend on has exactly one supplier. Find second sources, qualify them properly with the science team, and keep them warm, so that switching is a decision we make rather than an emergency we react to. Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back. Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line. Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it. Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it. Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after. Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter. Own COGS with Finance. Procurement and finance are the two halves of gross margin, and you are the procurement half. Automate the whole thing. Ordering, tracking, and reconciliation should mostly run themselves. What We're Looking For You have worked in supply chain or procurement in a physical, technical business. Biotech, a CRO, or another life science company is ideal, and you understand reagent categories — enzymes, antibodies, media, resins, plasticware — and how they are actually sourced. Hardware manufacturing or another high-mix production setting translates well. Buying software licences does not. You do not need to have run a supply chain organization before; you do need to be ready to own one. You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up. You are technical enough to talk to scientists. You do not need a degree in biology, but you will be qualifying an alternative supplier for a reagent that a protein biochemist depends on, and you need to be able to have that conversation properly rather than forwarding it. You can negotiate. Comfortable sitting across from vendors who have been selling into labs for thirty years, and comfortable walking away. You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. Some of our largest suppliers still require a human to upload a spreadsheet to a portal, and we consider that a bug rather than a fact of life. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other. Obsessive about the details that bite. Lead times, expiry dates, lot numbers, minimum order quantities. Nothing falls through. You want to grow fast. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year, and the lab spend grows faster than the headcount does. Swiss or EU import/export experience is a strong plus. Scope We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a spreadsheet with Finance, on the phone with a courier, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing. That is the deal, and if it sounds unappealing then we are probably not the right place. What we do want to be clear about is where the centre of gravity is. This role is about what we buy, who we buy it from, what we pay, and how reliably it turns up. Sourcing, negotiation, supplier relationships, inventory, resilience, cost. Plenty of other things will land on your desk and you should take them, but that is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on. One thing it is not: an order-taking job. You are not a mailbox between scientists and vendors. You decide what we source and from whom, and we expect you to argue with us about it. Why This Role Is Interesting Most supply chain jobs are about keeping a stable system stable. This one is about building the supply chain for a lab that is about to grow several-fold, at a company where the cost and reliability of an experiment more or less is the product. Every franc you take out of the cost of a protein, and every week you take out of a lead time, shows up directly in what we can offer customers and in whether AI-designed biology is cheap enough to be worth doing at scale. There are not many procurement jobs where the leverage is that direct, or that visible to the people running the company. Application deadline We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis. title: AI Builder — Working Student
description: EggAI Labs · Working Student · In Person (Tübingen, Germany) Designing lifecycle evaluation for nondeterministic domain-specific AI systems. EggAI Labs We're opening the EggAI Labs in Tübingen. The Labs purpose is to test new AI capabilities, identify what works, how they'd improve delivery, and then build assets to support teams and clients. EggAI's mission cannot be achieved through one-off client projects alone and the Labs is the way to adapt and scale. As part of the first cohort, you will join a small peer group and work directly with EggAI's CAIO, a Tübingen alumnus. You will also collaborate with our engineering, product, and project leads, who will bring you insights from client problems, help you understand their context and challenge your solutions for them. Your fellow AI Builders will be deliberately chosen to span different passions and strenghts. You will have room to explore and be expected to turn that exploration into something useful. This is not a client-facing role. The problem: EvalOps How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions? We will explore EvalOps : the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way. These questions will guide the initial work: Regression suites : How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales? Coverage estimation : How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors? Live monitoring : Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals? Eval analysis : How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions. The role As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice: Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype. Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work. Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence. Communicate decisions and learning clearly. Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve. Code and build end to end. This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars. Three pillars, different passions Pillar Driving question Possible EvalOps focus Product What should we build? Workflows and interfaces that help domain experts create evals, inspect traces, understand results, and make decisions. Engineering How should we build it? Dependable and scalable evaluation infrastructure, trace processing, monitoring, and governance tooling. Data Science How do we know it works? Coverage measures, sampling strategies, scoring methods, statistical tests, anomaly detection, and reasoning under uncertainty. We expect every AI Builder to develop a practical foundation across all three pillars and to pursue greater depth in the one that most strongly matches their passion. What we value Problem obsession . A difficult question captures your curiosity. You keep returning to it, pursue ideas without waiting for instructions, and care deeply about finding an answer that works. Initiative and follow-through . You turn uncertainty into something you can investigate, test, and improve—and stay resourceful when the first approach fails. Evidence of making things work . Show us something you created, the decisions you made, and what you learned along the way. Independent judgment . You test new capabilities yourself, distinguish evidence from enthusiasm, and change your mind when the findings warrant it. Generosity in collaboration . You explain your thinking, seek candid feedback, act on it, and help others make progress. What is required You are pursuing a Master’s degree. You can write code and turn an idea into working, tested software. You can work from Tübingen and communicate fluently in English, our company language. Relevant fields include Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Bioinformatics, Computational Neuroscience, Medical Informatics, Quantitative Data Science, Cognitive Science. We also welcome candidates from other disciplines who can demonstrate strong problem-solving and practical technical ability. What you will gain Industry insight . Learn what works and what breaks in real enterprise AI systems, with access to problems from EggAI’s client work Meaningful ownership . Take an EvalOps problem from investigation to a working, evaluated solution, with freedom to shape the approach. Close mentorship . Work directly with EggAI’s Chief AI Officer and sharpen your judgment through feedback from engineering, product, and project leads. Room to develop . Deepen your strengths, learn from peers with complementary perspectives, and use modern AI-development tools on unresolved problems. A say in the Lab’s direction . Help establish its working practices, propose new questions, and influence what it pursues next. Competitive compensation , including recognition for exceptional contributions, and a potential path to a full-time EggAI role after graduation. How to apply A short cover letter is required. Your CV tells us what you have done so far, but we're also interested in the why . Use the letter to explain why you made those choices, what drives you, and why the AI Builder role at EggAI Labs feels like the right next step in your career. We are looking for exceptional students, and excellence takes many forms, e.g., academic results, research or ambitious projects. Whatever form yours takes, show us the appropriate evidence, be it grades, publications, something you've built or other evidence of impact. This is an in-person role in Tübingen. We can only consider candidates who live within commuting distance. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Doctorant(e) "Développement et caractérisation d’une plateforme multi-capteurs pour le monitoring de sites de stockage onshore de CO2" - Contrat doctoral
description: ENGLISH VERSION Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain. Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif. L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain. À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École. Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques. Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret. Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité. Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins. L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité. 🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’ industrie du futur. Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ? 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous En tant que doctorant, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions de recherche et innovation et, dans une moindre mesure de nos missions d’enseignement. Vous serez affecté au centre SPIN – LGF (Laboratoire Georges Friedel, UMR CNRS 5307). Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal. Le centre SPIN (Science des Procédés Industriels et Naturels), qui sera fortement impliqué dans la thèse, développe, au sein de Mines Saint-Etienne, son expertise dans le domaine du Génie des Procédés appliqué aux systèmes dispersés : grains, particules, gouttes, bulles, milieux poreux. Il possède également des compétences en développement de capteurs et d’instrumentation. Les technologies de captage et stockage du CO2 sont des technologies clés pour la décarbonation du secteur industriel. Les stockages offshores ont déjà démontré leur faisabilité, mais les stockages onshores semblent nécessaires pour augmenter les capacités de stockage tout en réduisant le transport de CO2. Or, la proximité de ces sites avec les populations rend leurs déploiements incertains et soulève des questions relatives à l’acceptabilité sociale. La surveillance à long terme des sites de stockage de CO2, exigée par la directive européenne CCS, constitue une opportunité pour renforcer la transparence et l’acceptation locale du stockage en engageant les parties prenantes dans l’acquisition et l’interprétation des données. Cependant, les systèmes actuels de surveillance ne permettent pas à la fois de réaliser des mesures in-situ, simulations numériques et visualisation interactive pour une approche du suivi intégrée des sites de stockage. Le projet CO2MET vise à développer et faire progresser des unités ou éléments clés pour préparer un futur système intégré de surveillance numérique à long terme améliorant la fiabilité et l’acceptabilité du stockage géologique de CO2. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le consortium CO2MET a été constitué et est composé de l'IFPEN, du BRGM, de Mines Saint-Etienne et de Cerema. La surveillance à long terme nécessite des outils fiables et performants, notamment dans le domaine des capteurs environnementaux, ce qui soulève la question de la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives pour traiter le signal, ainsi que celle de l'influence des variations à long terme des paramètres externes sur la réponse des capteurs (et de l'impact du changement climatique). Étant donné que les signaux de concentration en CO₂ peuvent, à eux seuls, ne pas être suffisamment discriminants (les concentrations biologiques dans les sols pouvant dépasser 10 % vol.), compte tenu de leurs origines diverses (sources profondes, provenant du stockage ou de l’interaction gaz-roche ; processus de respiration ; oxydation du méthane), la prévention des faux positifs dans la surveillance des sites de stockage doit s'appuyer sur des capteurs de CO₂ (NDIR ou photoacoustiques) et sur d'autres capteurs (par exemple, un capteur chimique d'O₂), ainsi que sur des capteurs environnementaux (humidité, pression, température) afin de permettre une attribution correcte de la source de CO2. Parmi les missions qui lui seront attribuées, le doctorant devra : · Sélectionner des capteurs existants répondants aux spécifications afin de mettre au point une plateforme de détection · Etudier, en conditions de laboratoire, la sélectivité des capteurs vis-à-vis des espèces gazeuses interférentes, à l’aide d’une analyse multivariée · Définir des algorithmes de prédiction tenant compte de la reproductibilité, de la dérive, de la linéarité et de la variabilité dans des mélanges gazeux complexes et des conditions environnementales variables (température, pression et humidité relative) · Etudier l'influence du vieillissement des capteurs sur leur réponse et sur les prévisions établies, afin de proposer un algorithme de compensation · Enfin, mener des études de cas concrets sur le site de Sainte-Marguerite (Puy-de-Dôme), avec des niveaux d'émissions de CO₂ variables, afin de tester et de valider les plateformes de capteurs développées. Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer enseignement, recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir. 🔍 Ce que nous recherchons Vous êtes titulaire d’un : · Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent Et idéalement : · Titulaire d’un de master 2 dans les domaines suivants : Mesure / Instrumentation / Métrologie ; Acquisition, traitement et analyse de la donnée · Avec une expérience de stage ou professionnelle dans la recherche (goût prononcé pour la partie expérimentale) · Junior accepté : oui Vos atouts supplémentaires : • La thématique du sujet étant multidisciplinaire de solides connaissances en instrumentations / capteurs, traitements de données, analyse multivariée seront nécessaires. D’autres part, des connaissances en probabilités / statistiques seront également appréciées. • Le sujet comporte un volet expérimental important mais de solides connaissances numériques seront utiles pour la partie traitement des données (notamment codage sur python) • Aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite (notamment en langue anglaise) 🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ? Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde . Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver : · Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain · Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an · Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail. Mines Saint-Étienne, école de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, assure des missions de formation, de recherche, d’innovation et de transfert industriel. Avec 2 500 élèves, 500 personnels et un budget de 50 M€, elle dispose de trois campus spécialisés. Sa stratégie 2023-2027 vise à accompagner les transitions écologique, numérique et générationnelle, tout en contribuant à la souveraineté nationale et européenne en microélectronique et numérique. Le campus Aix-Marseille-Provence, situé à Gardanne, regroupe le Centre Microélectronique de Provence (CMP), des formations d’ingénieurs et de masters, un incubateur technologique et des plateformes de prototypage. Il accueille environ 400 étudiants et 200 personnels de Mines Saint-Étienne et d’entreprises partenaires. Le CMP dispose d’une salle blanche de 700 m², équipée d’une centaine d’équipements scientifiques répartis en zones de classes 100, 1 000 et 10 000. Cette plateforme est utilisée par les équipes de recherche, les membres académiques et industriels de l’association Micro-PackS, ainsi que pour les formations initiales et continues. Ses activités couvrent notamment les procédés de couches minces, la photolithographie, la chimie, la caractérisation physique et électrique des matériaux et dispositifs, le micropackaging, l’électronique imprimée et la préparation d’échantillons. 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous Dans le cadre du projet I-novmicro porté par le Campus des Métiers et des Qualifications Industrie du Futur, des modules de formation aux procédés de fabrication en microélectronique sont proposés à des étudiants et apprenants en formation initiale ou continue. La formation se concentrera sur la réalisation de transistor NMOS. Le Centre de Microélectronique de Provence recrute un ingénieur pour mettre en place et dispenser ces formations, gérer les opérations nécessaires au bon déroulement de celles-ci. Vos Missions : Achat d’équipements La personne retenue gérera, dans un premier temps, l’achat de nouveaux équipements destinés aux formations décrites en introduction. Mise en place de la formation La personne sera chargée de développer le module de formation sur le transistor NMOS, en ciblant certains procédés de fabrication. Elle assurera ensuite l’animation des sessions de formation aux procédés microélectroniques associées à ce module. Ainsi, la personne recrutée devra être former aux procédés standard utilisés en microélectronique (front-end), et effectuer les étapes de fabrication de composants, développées dans le cadre des formations dispensées. Elle sera également en charge du développement de nouveaux procédés. Dans le cadre de ces missions, la ou le titulaire du poste devra utiliser des produits chimiques, et donc en gérer les aspects sécurité. Elle devra utiliser des équipements de caractérisation (ex : microscopie, ellipsométrie, profilométrie) dans le cadre des formations dispensées, et devra pouvoir former des utilisateurs à ces techniques. Recherche Etant associé aux départements de recherche du CMP, notamment le département d’électronique flexible, des activités complémentaires de recherche sont envisageables. 🔍 Ce que nous recherchons Les candidates et candidats doivent être titulaires au minimum d’un bac+5, et avoir une expérience dans la microélectronique, en process et caractérisation en salle blanche. Une forte polyvalence est requise pour ce poste, avec notamment des compétences en : Procédés (connaissance et maîtrise) : photolithographie, gravure humide et sèche, dépôts de couches minces et traitements thermiques, Caractérisation physique de matériaux et dispositifs, et caractérisation électrique de dispositifs. Une expérience dans le domaine de la formation technique est un réel atout. Les qualités requises pour le poste sont la pédagogie, l’autonomie, la rigueur, la méthode et l’organisation dans le travail, l’habileté technique et une aisance en communication orale et écrite. La personne retenue devra montrer d’excellentes capacités d’analyse, faire preuve de pragmatisme et d’initiative, avoir l’esprit d’équipe, montrer des qualités relationnelles, et avoir le sens du service. La pratique de l’anglais est nécessaire, notamment pour la communication avec les équipementiers ou avec certains utilisateurs anglophones de la salle blanche. 🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ? Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde. Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver : · Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain · Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an · Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens. 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant ! 🔗 Les dossiers de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, lettre de recommandation le cas échéant, pièce d’identité) sont à déposer sur la plateforme RECRUITEE avant le 1er décembre 2026 : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/o/une-ingenieure-ou-un-ingenieur-procedes-et-formation-en-salle-blanche-microelectronique-centre-microelectronique-de-provence-cdd-2-ans Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description: Our Company "Buying Labs is the leading global partner for sourcing and distributing premium consumer goods!" We're looking for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer (m/f/d) to join our Tech team at our Hamburg headquarters. Our goal is to supercharge how our business works with AI and technology, wherever it makes a real difference. You'll build the systems our teams rely on every day, from internal applications to the data and AI capabilities behind them, and see the impact of your work directly in the business. This is a role for an experienced engineer who takes real ownership: someone who designs solid systems, builds AI into them where it adds value, and drives their work through to production and real users. Your Mission Own systems end to end: Design, build and run features across frontend and backend, from technical approach through deployment and support in production. Build AI into our products: Design and integrate AI-powered features such as structured extraction, classification, automation and agentic workflows. Make them reliable through validation, evaluation and human review where it matters. Data modelling and architecture: Build solid data models in PostgreSQL that serve as the foundation for our applications and AI features. Make architecture decisions that keep our systems maintainable as they grow. Modern and established codebases: Build new applications on our modern stack, and maintain and modernise our established JavaScript platform, which our teams rely on every day. Quality you can stand behind: Write tested, reviewed code and verify your own work before it reaches users. Monitor and troubleshoot production issues. Work closely with the business: Understand the processes behind what you build, work directly with our commercial and operational teams, and help shape what gets built and why. Raise the bar: Share knowledge, Your Profile 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of building and running production applications end to end. Proven experience building AI into production systems or applications, for example LLM-based extraction or classification, RAG, or agentic and tool-use workflows. You know how to make AI output reliable through validation, evaluation and fallbacks. Using AI coding assistants alone does not meet this requirement. You use AI tools in your daily development work and have solid habits for checking and reviewing what they produce. Strong TypeScript and JavaScript, and modern React, including hooks and state management. Strong backend experience with Node.js and Express or a comparable framework, REST APIs, and integrating external systems. Deep PostgreSQL and SQL skills, with solid data modelling and experience with an ORM or query builder such as Knex, Sequelize or Prisma. Comfortable working across both modern TypeScript applications and an established JavaScript codebase. Strong quality mindset: automated testing, code reviews, and taking responsibility for what you ship. High ownership and drive: you push your work through to done, raise problems early, and don't wait to be told what to do next. Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience. Fluent English required; German is a plus. Based in Hamburg or willing to relocate. Nice to Have Depth in LLM tooling: provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), agent and tool-use patterns (MCP), and evaluating output quality. Vector search (pgvector or similar). Product or process awareness: experience understanding how a business works and turning messy processes into structured systems. Experience integrating ERPs or operational systems (orders, inventory, master data). Our wider stack: Bun, Vite, Redis, RabbitMQ, Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS. Observability and product analytics tools (e.g. Sentry, Datadog, PostHog). Python for data tooling. Background in eCommerce, wholesale or B2B environments. Why Us? An awesome team & great vibes: Work with motivated colleagues in an agile, ambitious, and friendly atmosphere where collaboration and fun go hand in hand with high speed. Flat hierarchies & real growth opportunities: Take ownership of your role and develop personally alongside the company. We promote from within and value every voice, regardless of seniority or title. Modern workplace & cutting-edge equipment: State-of-the-art office setup including adjustable desks, mobile treadmills, air conditioning, and everything you need to excel in your role. Company pension program (bAV): Smart pension plan with a 30% Buying Labs grant on your contribution, investing in your financial future together. Corporate Benefits membership: Access exclusive discounts from a wide range of partner brands and retailers. Full "Deutschlandticket" coverage: We cover the complete cost (ca. €60/month) so you can travel sustainably and conveniently throughout Germany. Free bike options: Choose between a complimentary "Swapfiets" bike (original or deluxe 7) or opt for JobRad bike-leasing with an additional €26/month grant from Buying Labs. Complimentary food & beverages: Free Friday lunch in the office, plus organic fruit & vegetables, drinks, snacks, coffee/tea, healthy shots and seasonal treats (e.g. ice cream, soups) throughout the week. Personalized workspace setup: €100 welcome voucher to customize and optimize your workspace from day one. Refer-A-Friend (employee referral program): You love being part of Buying Labs? Fantastic! Then recommend people from your personal network and receive attractive rewards. Sounds like a perfect fit? We can't wait to meet you. Apply now and be part of our journey!
